rule.reason: Both roles are published in Head, Paun and Pixton (Handbook of Formal Languages vol. 2, ch. 7) and both are declared in the same iterated-closure region: the splicing-rule separator inside rule words u1#u2$u3#u4, and the dummy index $ marking a word born in the original input (as in F_$(s,$)). The body declares the second typed role explicitly and the dummy index can never equal a rule word, so the argument type disambiguates the glyph.

Gunter's PCF presentation uses the same arrow both for the simple type constructor s -> t (def:p10-oa-language) and for the small-step relation M -> N (def:p10-oa-evaluation, which declares it before the literal rule input). Both are declared in the same region; type operands s,t versus term operands M,N fix the reading, so the source glyph is retained rather than splitting the region.
